examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Real or Imaginary Part of a Scalar Given the Conjugate of a Scaled Vector
examples.worked_solution:
Since $\overline{k\mathbf{v}} = \overline{k} \, \overline{\mathbf{v}},$ we get the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{kv} & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{v} \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-4\text{i} \\ 0\end{aligned}]} \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{0}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}4\text{i} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4\text{i}\,\overset{―}{k} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain that 

$$
4\textrm{i}\,\overline{k}  = 8\textrm{i}-12
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
\overline{k}=\dfrac{8\textrm{i}-12}{4\textrm i} = 2+3\textrm{i}.
$$

 

Therefore, $k=\overline{2+3\textrm{i}}=2-3\textrm{i}.$

Finally, $\textrm{Im}(k)=-3.$

feedback.problem: If $\,\text{Re}(x)=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\text{Im}(x)=[\begin{aligned}c \\ d\end{aligned}]\,$ are the real and imaginary parts of the vector $\,x=[\begin{aligned}2+4\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ then what is the value of $ad+bc?$
feedback.worked_solution:
For the given vector $\,x=[\begin{aligned}2+4\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =[\begin{aligned}2+4\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(x)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $\,a=2,b=5,c=4$ and $d=-2$, which implies that 

$$
ad+bc=2\cdot (-2)+5\cdot 4=16.
$$
